# 16-Week Half Marathon Training Plan (Intermediate Level)

## Plan Overview

**Target Audience:** Runners with 1-2 years consistent running, 30-35 mpw base
**Goal:** Half Marathon (13.1 miles) in 16 weeks
**Weekly Mileage:** 23-61 miles (peak week 61)
**Experience Required:** Comfortable running 60+ minutes continuously, completed at least one 10K race

### If This Is More Volume Than You Want

This plan peaks at **61 miles** in its biggest week. That is a real half marathon build, and
it sits at the top of the intermediate range rather than the middle of it. Every weekly
total in this plan has been checked against the workouts actually listed underneath it,
so the number above is the number you will run.

**To run this plan at roughly 50 miles per week instead:**

- Trim **5-6 miles per week off the easy days only**. Take a mile off two or three easy
  runs rather than a large chunk off one.
- **Do not cut the quality sessions** (tempo, intervals, marathon-pace work). They are the
  reason the plan works.
- **Do not cut the long run** by more than a mile or two. It is the other reason.
- If the plan still feels like too much after that, you want the beginner version, not a
  trimmed version of this one. There is no shame in that and it will make you faster than
  limping through a plan that is over your head.

The volume is a dial. The easy/hard structure is not. See
[Training Principles](../fundamentals/training-principles.md) and
[Injury Prevention](../fundamentals/injury-prevention.md).

## Before You Start

1. **Determine Your Current Fitness:**
   - Run a 10K time trial OR
   - Use recent 5K or 10K race time
   - Enter into McMillan or VDOT calculator

2. **Know Your Training Paces:**
   - **Easy:** Conversational pace (Zone 2, 60-70% max HR)
   - **Marathon Pace (MP):** Steady effort (Zone 3, 70-80% max HR)
   - **Tempo:** Comfortably hard (~10K-HM race pace, Zone 4, 80-90% max HR)
   - **Interval:** Hard effort (~5K race pace, Zone 5, 90-100% max HR)
   - **Half Marathon Pace (HMP):** Goal race pace

3. **Schedule Your Race:**
   - Pick your goal half marathon for Week 16
   - Optional: tune-up 10K race in Week 12

## Training Philosophy

The half marathon is the perfect balance of speed and endurance. This plan emphasizes:

- **Weeks 1-6:** Base building (volume and aerobic development)
- **Weeks 7-12:** Build phase (tempo work and threshold development)
- **Weeks 13-15:** Peak phase (race-specific training)
- **Week 16:** Taper and race

**Key focus:** Lactate threshold development + long run endurance + race pace practice

## The 16-Week Plan

### Phase 1: Base Building (Weeks 1-6)

#### Week 1: Establish Base (39-42 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 5 miles
- **Tuesday:** Easy 6 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Rest or easy 3 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 12 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 2: Build Volume (45 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** Easy 6 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 13 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 3: Increase Volume (47 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** Easy 7 miles + 8x100m strides
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 14 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 4: Recovery Week (30 miles)
- **Monday:** Rest
- **Tuesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 4 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Rest
- **Saturday:** Long run 10 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 4 miles

#### Week 5: Build Again (50 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** Easy 7 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 15 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 6: Recovery Week (33 miles)
- **Monday:** Rest
- **Tuesday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Rest
- **Saturday:** Long run 11 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 4 miles

---

### Phase 2: Build - Add Tempo & Quality (Weeks 7-12)

#### Week 7: Introduce Tempo (48 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** **Tempo** - 2mi warmup + 20 min at tempo pace + 2mi cooldown = 8 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 14 miles (last 3 at marathon pace)
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 8: Build Tempo (52 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** **Tempo** - 2mi warmup + 25 min at tempo pace + 2mi cooldown = 9 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 15 miles (middle 5 at marathon pace)
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 9: Extended Tempo (55 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** **Tempo** - 2mi warmup + 5mi at tempo pace + 2mi cooldown = 11 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Saturday:** Long run 16 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 10: Recovery Week (35 miles)
- **Monday:** Rest
- **Tuesday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Rest
- **Saturday:** Long run 12 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 11: Add Intervals (51 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** **Intervals** - 2mi warmup + 5x1200m at 5K pace w/3min rest + 2mi cooldown = 10 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Saturday:** **Tempo Long Run** - 2mi easy + 30 min tempo + 2mi easy + 3mi easy = 12 miles
- **Sunday:** Recovery 6 miles

#### Week 12: Recovery + Optional 10K Race (23-35 miles)
- **Monday:** Rest
- **Tuesday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 5 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Thursday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Friday:** Rest
- **Saturday:** **OPTIONAL: 10K race** OR long run 12 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

---

### Phase 3: Peak - Race-Specific Training (Weeks 13-15)

#### Week 13: Half Marathon Pace Introduction (58 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Tuesday:** **HMP Run** - 2mi warmup + 6mi at half marathon pace + 2mi cooldown = 12 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 5 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Saturday:** **Long Run** - 17 miles (first 13 easy, last 4 at HMP)
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

#### Week 14: Peak Mileage (61 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Tuesday:** **Tempo** - 2mi warmup + 6mi at tempo pace + 2mi cooldown = 12 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 5 miles + 8x100m strides
- **Saturday:** **Long Run** - 18 miles (first 10 easy, middle 6 at marathon pace, last 2 easy)
- **Sunday:** Recovery 6 miles

#### Week 15: Final Quality Week (58 miles)
- **Monday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Tuesday:** **Race Simulation** - 2mi warmup + 10mi at half marathon pace + 2mi cooldown = 16 miles
- **Wednesday:** Easy 6 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 7 miles
- **Friday:** Easy 4 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Saturday:** Long run 13 miles easy
- **Sunday:** Recovery 5 miles

---

### Phase 4: Taper (Week 16)

#### Week 16: Taper Week (24 miles + race)
- **Monday:** Easy 5 miles
- **Tuesday:** Easy 5 miles + 6x100m strides
- **Wednesday:** **Sharpener** - 2mi easy + 3mi at tempo + 3min rest + 6x400m at 5K pace w/90sec rest + 1mi easy = 7 miles
- **Thursday:** Easy 4 miles
- **Friday:** Rest
- **Saturday:** Easy 3 miles with 4x100m strides OR rest
- **Sunday:** **RACE DAY! Half Marathon** 🏁

---

## Workout Descriptions

### Easy Runs
- **Pace:** Conversational, full sentences
- **HR:** Zone 2 (60-70% max)
- **Purpose:** Build aerobic base, recovery
- **Note:** Should feel genuinely easy

### Strides
- **Distance:** 100 meters
- **Pace:** Smooth acceleration to mile pace
- **Recovery:** Walk back
- **Purpose:** Form, neuromuscular coordination
- **Frequency:** 2-3x per week

### Marathon Pace (MP) Runs
- **Pace:** Steady effort, 30-45 sec/mile slower than tempo
- **HR:** Zone 3 (70-80% max)
- **Purpose:** Build aerobic endurance at faster pace
- **Note:** Important for half marathon - it's slightly easier than race pace

### Tempo Runs (Threshold Pace)
- **Pace:** "Comfortably hard" - roughly 10K to HM race pace
- **HR:** Zone 4 (80-90% max)
- **Feel:** Can speak 3-5 words
- **Purpose:** Improve lactate threshold (CRITICAL FOR HALF MARATHON)
- **Note:** Most important workout type for this distance

### Half Marathon Pace (HMP) Runs
- **Pace:** Goal half marathon race pace
- **Purpose:** Train body/mind for race effort, practice fueling
- **Note:** Practice race-day nutrition and pacing

### Intervals (VO2 Max Pace)
- **Pace:** 5K race pace
- **HR:** Zone 5 (90-100% max)
- **Purpose:** Maintain speed and VO2 max
- **Note:** Secondary to tempo work for half marathon

### Long Runs
- **Types:**
  - Easy long runs: All easy pace
  - MP long runs: Sections at marathon pace
  - HMP long runs: Final miles at half marathon pace
- **Purpose:** Build endurance, mental toughness, race specificity
- **Peak:** 18 miles (Week 14)

### Recovery Runs
- **Pace:** Very easy, slower than easy pace
- **Purpose:** Active recovery
- **Note:** Especially after long runs and tempo workouts

## Half Marathon Racing Strategy

### Race Week:
- **7 days out:** Last hard workout (Wednesday)
- **5-6 days out:** Easy running only
- **2-3 days out:** Short easy run with strides
- **1-2 days out:** Rest or very short shakeout

### Race Day Warm-Up:
- 10-15 min easy jog
- 6-8x100m strides
- Dynamic stretches
- Bathroom break
- Line up 5-10 min before start

### Race Pacing Strategy:

**Conservative Strategy (Recommended for First Half):**
- **Miles 1-3:** 5-10 sec/mile SLOWER than goal pace (resist the crowd!)
- **Miles 4-10:** Settle into goal pace, find rhythm
- **Miles 11-12:** Push the pace if feeling good
- **Mile 13 + 0.1:** Empty the tank, strong finish

**Even Pace Strategy (Experienced Runners):**
- Target even splits throughout
- Slight negative split if possible
- Save energy for final 5K push

**Common Pacing Mistakes:**
- Going out too fast (most common!)
- Not accounting for hills in early miles
- Ignoring effort level on warm/windy days

### Fueling Strategy:
- **Pre-race:** Light meal 2-3 hours before (test in training)
- **During race:**
  - Most runners: Water/sports drink at aid stations
  - 1:30+ finish time: Consider 1-2 gels (Mile 6 and 10)
  - Practice in long runs!
- **Post-race:** Carbs + protein within 30-60 min

### Post-Race Recovery:
- Cool-down: 10-15 min easy walk/jog
- Easy running only for 5-7 days
- No hard workouts for 10-14 days
- Rule of thumb: 1 day easy for every mile raced (13 days)

## Customization Guidelines

### If You're New to This Distance:
- Start with 30-32 mpw base instead of 35
- Reduce long runs by 1-2 miles
- Focus on completing plan, not hitting exact paces
- Don't add extra miles or workouts

### If You're More Advanced:
- Can start at Week 3-4 if coming off solid base
- Can add 3-5 miles to weekly total
- Can extend long runs by 1-2 miles (max 20 miles)
- Don't exceed 50 mpw for this plan

### If You Miss a Workout:
1. **Easy run:** Skip it
2. **Long run:** Reschedule within same week if possible
3. **Tempo run:** Most important - try to reschedule
4. **Intervals:** Can skip, less critical for half marathon
5. **Never:** Double up quality days

### If You're Too Tired:
- Make hard workout an easy run
- Take extra rest day
- Check if easy runs are truly easy
- Recovery > single workout

## Training Intensity Distribution

**This plan follows 80/20:**
- ~75% easy running (Zones 1-2)
- ~15% tempo/threshold (Zone 4)
- ~5% marathon pace (Zone 3)
- ~5% intervals (Zone 5)

The half marathon is primarily a **lactate threshold race**, so tempo work is heavily emphasized.

## Key Long Run Progression

```
Week 1:  12 miles (easy)
Week 2:  13 miles (easy)
Week 3:  14 miles (easy)
Week 4:  10 miles (recovery)
Week 5:  15 miles (easy)
Week 6:  11 miles (recovery)
Week 7:  14 miles (3mi MP finish)
Week 8:  15 miles (5mi MP middle)
Week 9:  16 miles (easy)
Week 10: 12 miles (recovery)
Week 11: 12 miles (tempo embedded)
Week 12: 12 miles (easy or 10K race)
Week 13: 17 miles (4mi HMP finish)
Week 14: 18 miles (6mi MP middle) ← PEAK
Week 15: 13 miles (easy)
Week 16: RACE (13.1 miles)
```

## Weekly Mileage Progression

```
Week 1: 39-42 miles
Week 2: 45 miles
Week 3: 47 miles
Week 4: 30 miles (recovery)
Week 5: 50 miles
Week 6: 33 miles (recovery)
Week 7: 48 miles
Week 8: 52 miles
Week 9: 55 miles
Week 10: 35 miles (recovery)
Week 11: 51 miles
Week 12: 23-35 miles (recovery/race)
Week 13: 58 miles
Week 14: 61 miles (PEAK)
Week 15: 58 miles
Week 16: 24 miles + race (taper)
```

## Success Tips

1. **Long runs are crucial** - Don't skip these
2. **Tempo runs build race fitness** - Your most important workout
3. **Practice race pace** - Get comfortable with HMP in Weeks 13-15
4. **Nail your fueling** - Test nutrition strategy in training
5. **Don't go out too fast** - Hardest lesson to learn
6. **Respect the taper** - Trust your training in final 2 weeks
7. **Stay consistent** - Better to do 90% healthy than 110% injured
8. **Sleep matters** - 7-9 hours nightly

## Mental Training

The half marathon is as much mental as physical:
- **Miles 1-7:** Stay patient, resist going too fast
- **Miles 7-10:** This is where the race really starts, stay focused
- **Miles 10-13:** Mental toughness matters, embrace the discomfort
- **Practice mental strategies in long runs**
- **Break race into 5K segments**

## Expected Adaptations

By end of this plan:
- Significantly improved lactate threshold
- Enhanced endurance for 90+ minute efforts
- Better running economy
- Improved fat oxidation
- Mental toughness for distance racing
- Race-specific fitness for 13.1 miles

## Additional Resources

- **Lactate Threshold:** See `/concepts/lactate-threshold.md`
- **Long Run Training:** See `/fundamentals/workout-types.md`
- **Periodization:** See `/visuals/periodization-guide.md`
- **Training Systems:** See `/systems/comparison.md`
- **Heart Rate Zones:** See `/visuals/heart-rate-zones-table.md`

---

Good luck with your half marathon training! The half marathon is a beautiful distance - long enough to be a real challenge, short enough to race hard. Master your threshold, build your endurance, and execute your race plan. You've got this! 🏃‍♀️💪
